architectural_implications.after: An AGENTS.md / skill file holds anti-pattern gates plus a theme library, applied automatically to every generation.
architectural_implications.before: Each prompt restates style preferences as adjectives; quality depends on who wrote the prompt and when.
architectural_implications.consequence: Taste becomes diffable, reviewable, and A/B-testable; regressions in aesthetics become attributable to config changes, and the artifact must be maintained and de-duplicated with prompt text.
architectural_implications.observation: Design constraints move from per-request prompt text into a repo-level, versioned config artifact loaded into the agent environment.

architectural_implications.after: Retrieval of multiple admired exemplar screenshots injected into the generation context.
architectural_implications.before: Text-only prompts describing the desired aesthetic.
architectural_implications.consequence: Requires asset curation, licensing/attribution handling, and context-budget management; also introduces an evaluation question of which exemplars caused which improvement.
architectural_implications.observation: A curated screenshot/reference store becomes part of context infrastructure rather than ad-hoc paste.

architectural_implications.after: Cheap, fast open-source model drives the high-frequency iteration loop; expensive models reserved where a measured quality delta justifies them.
architectural_implications.before: One frontier closed model used for all generation and refinement turns.
architectural_implications.consequence: Needs cross-model equivalence evals and prompt/constraint portability, since constraint packs tuned for one model family may not transfer.
architectural_implications.observation: Model choice becomes per-phase routing inside the agent harness rather than a single product-wide decision.

architectural_implications.after: A queued sequence of incremental messages, each building on the last, with checkpoints between steps.
architectural_implications.before: One monolithic prompt requesting the entire app in a single shot.
architectural_implications.consequence: Adds orchestration and state machinery (queue, checkpoints, rollback) but creates natural points for per-step verification and reduces blast radius of a bad generation.
architectural_implications.observation: Long-horizon build tasks are executed as an ordered milestone queue with foundation-first sequencing.

article_ideas.angle: Frame anti-pattern gates as the aesthetic analogue of guardrails and refusals: the same enforcement pattern applied to quality rather than safety, with the same escape-hatch and over-constraint risks.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers building generation pipelines and agent harnesses
article_ideas.thesis: Style adjectives are unverifiable prompt noise; enumerated forbidden outputs are checkable, diffable, and enforceable at generation time. The durable abstraction for generative quality is a blacklist of recognizable anti-patterns, not an adjectival request to 'make it beautiful' — and this transfers to docs, API schemas, and error messages, not just UI.
article_ideas.title: Stop Describing Good Taste. Enumerate Bad Output.

article_ideas.angle: Configuration-as-capability argument: relocate the quality contract from model weights and prompt craft into a reviewable repo artifact, and show what breaks (maintenance, de-duplication with prompt text, per-model transfer).
article_ideas.audience: Platform and DevEx teams standardizing agent configuration
article_ideas.based_on: Design taste is packaged as a portable context artifact
article_ideas.thesis: When quality lives in a versioned constraint-and-theme artifact injected into agent context rather than in scattered prompt wording, aesthetic regressions become attributable to a config change and model swaps become cheap because the quality contract travels with the repo. Teams that keep taste in chat history keep re-buying it every session.
article_ideas.title: The Aesthetic Regression Test: Putting Design in the Diff

article_ideas.angle: Measurement-first argument: distinguish 'constraints shift the mode' from 'constraints restore diversity' and show why the distinction decides whether design work is real or cosmetic.
article_ideas.based_on: Model output homogenization is a named, observable failure mode
article_ideas.thesis: When all outputs from a generative surface look alike, that sameness is a free, automatable quality signal — and, inversely, a fingerprint of default model behavior. Output similarity should be measured distributionally, because gating may only shift the mode rather than increase variance, producing a different shared style instead of genuine diversity.
article_ideas.title: Homogenization Is a Signal, Not Just a Complaint

article_ideas.angle: Contrarian benchmark critique grounded in loop economics; includes the caveat that single-task parity does not generalize to stateful UI.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leads making model-selection and routing decisions
article_ideas.based_on: GLM 5.2 reportedly matched or beat Opus 4.8 on landing-page generation
article_ideas.thesis: Aggregate model benchmarks mislead for iterative work because iteration is many-turn and exploratory. Route per phase — cheap fast models for the refine loop, frontier models only where a measured acceptance gap justifies them — and report quality-per-dollar-per-accepted-edit, since a weaker tier inside the loop compounds mediocre decisions across turns.
article_ideas.title: Cost-Per-Accepted-Change: The Only Benchmark Your Design Loop Needs

connections.relationship: Both enforce enumerated forbidden outputs at generation time; slop gates apply the guardrail pattern to aesthetics rather than safety.
A visual exemplar store is a retrieval index over demonstrations; the same context-budget and exemplar-selection problems apply.
Design constraints become versioned configuration colocated with the codebase, making aesthetics reviewable in the same diff as behavior.
Per-phase model tiering in an agent loop is a routing decision driven by measured quality-per-dollar rather than by aggregate benchmarks.
Enumerated anti-patterns are directly convertible into automated checks that gate or re-trigger generation, making taste an evaluable property.

evidence_quotes.text: Hallmark explicitly refuses gradient headers, three-card rows, fake testimonials, purple glows, and italicized title words.
Codifying design rules and anti-patterns into an AI skill file prevents models from using tired tropes.

core_insights.generalization: Any generative agent task with a strong default mode (UI, docs, API schemas, error messages, code structure) can be improved by enumerating the specific bad outputs to refuse rather than describing the desired good output.
core_insights.insight: Taste is best encoded as explicit negative constraints (anti-pattern 'slop gates') rather than positive stylistic adjectives. Hallmark enumerates forbidden outputs — gradient headers, three-card rows, fake testimonials, purple glows, italicized title words — which structurally removes the model's default repertoire instead of asking it to 'look good'.
core_insights.why_it_matters: Blacklists of specific, recognizable anti-patterns are checkable, diffable, and enforceable at generation time, whereas 'make it beautiful' is unverifiable. This is a general recipe for constraining any generative artifact where the model has a dominant low-quality prior.

evidence_quotes.text: A design skill framework that defines strict anti-patterns (slop gates) and provides a curated library of professional themes as context to AI models.
Giving AI models structured design themes and anti-patterns dramatically improves output quality in a single prompt.

core_insights.generalization: Wherever output quality is a product of taste rather than correctness, the durable abstraction is a declarative style/constraint pack loaded into agent context, not per-request prompt wording.
core_insights.insight: Design taste is packaged as a portable context artifact — a skill file combining anti-pattern gates with a curated theme library (Bubble, Distill, Cold Snap, Cinder), injected in a single prompt. Aesthetic capability is thus relocated from the model into versioned configuration.
core_insights.why_it_matters: If quality lives in a config artifact rather than in model weights or ad-hoc prompting, it can be reviewed, versioned, shared across a team, and A/B tested per model — and it makes model swaps cheaper because the quality contract travels with the repo.

evidence_quotes.text: Vibe-coded and AI-generated apps all look the same and share identical visual tells.
Purple gradient backgrounds
Scroll to explore badges

core_insights.generalization: Default-mode collapse applies to any high-frequency generative surface: if all outputs from an agent look alike, that sameness is both a UX liability and a cheap, automatable quality signal.
core_insights.insight: Model output homogenization is a named, observable failure mode: AI-generated apps converge on identical visual tells, so output similarity itself becomes a detectable signal of low-effort generation (and, inversely, of default model behavior).
core_insights.why_it_matters: Homogenization is measurable — an engineer can score a corpus of generations for shared tells. That turns 'AI slop' from a complaint into a metric: an anti-pattern detector that gates output or triggers regeneration, analogous to a linter for a deployed agent.

evidence_quotes.text: AI models perform significantly better when given concrete visual examples rather than abstract stylistic instructions.
Always feed your agent multiple reference screenshots of apps whose aesthetic you admire.

core_insights.generalization: For any task with a hard-to-verbalize target (layout, tone, code idiom, API ergonomics), exemplars are a higher-fidelity specification than adjectives, and the surrounding system should treat them as retrievable assets.
core_insights.insight: Concrete visual references outperform abstract style instructions: feeding multiple screenshots of admired apps produces substantially better results than describing an aesthetic in words.
core_insights.why_it_matters: This implies a context-supply problem, not a prompting problem: the harness needs a curated, retrievable asset store (an 'inspiration vault') and multimodality, so exemplars become infrastructure rather than something pasted ad hoc.

evidence_quotes.text: Smaller, faster open-source models like GLM 5.2 can match or beat expensive closed models for UI iteration at a fraction of the cost.
Smaller open-source models can generate design outputs comparable to expensive closed models at 5x lower cost and higher speed.

core_insights.generalization: In agentic loops, the model tier should be chosen per phase of the workflow (iterate vs. finalize vs. verify), not once per product.
core_insights.insight: Iteration economics favor small open-source models: GLM 5.2 reportedly matched or beat Opus 4.8 on landing-page generation at roughly 5x lower cost and higher speed, making high-frequency design iteration affordable on a cheap tier.
core_insights.why_it_matters: If design iteration is many-turn and exploratory, per-token cost and latency dominate the loop. That argues for a tiered router in the harness — cheap open-source model for the tight refine loop, frontier model only where a measured gap exists — plus cross-model equivalence evals so you know when the cheap tier is good enough.

evidence_quotes.text: Instead of demanding an entire app in one massive prompt, build the foundation and queue smaller incremental messages.
Queuing multiple incremental feature requests yields cleaner, more robust code and design than one monolithic prompt.

core_insights.generalization: Long-horizon generative tasks degrade as monolithic prompts grow; an explicit, checkpointed task queue is a structural fix that also improves inspectability and recoverability.
core_insights.insight: Decomposed, queued incremental prompts — foundation first, then a queue of small feature requests — reportedly yield cleaner, more robust code and design than one monolithic 'build the whole app' prompt.
core_insights.why_it_matters: This challenges the single-shot generation abstraction and implies the harness should own a milestone queue with per-step state, rather than one giant context window. It also creates natural checkpoints for regression checks and rollback.

evidence_quotes.text: Short, vague prompts lead to generic output; multi-paragraph prompts or voice notes provide necessary UX context.
Hassan records 2-3 minute voice notes detailing target user personas, UI components, and micro-interactions.

core_insights.generalization: Agents underperform on underspecified tasks; building an upstream capture step that externalizes intent into a durable spec is often higher leverage than downstream prompting tricks.
core_insights.insight: Intent capture is treated as spec authoring: 2-3 minute voice notes specifying target personas, UI components, and micro-interactions are fed as long prompts, converting vague requests into UX context.
core_insights.why_it_matters: It reframes the bottleneck as missing product specification rather than missing model capability — a workflow and tooling problem (voice-to-spec capture, durable spec artifacts) rather than a prompt-wording problem.

evidence_quotes.text: Vibe-coded and AI-generated apps all look the same and share identical visual tells.
Purple gradient backgrounds
Scroll to explore badges
All-caps pill buttons with dots
Recognizing AI visual clichés is the first step toward avoiding them and standing out competitively.

deep_dives.research_question: Can the enumerated visual tells of AI-generated UI (purple gradients, italicized header words, all-caps pill buttons, scroll-to-explore badges, gradient logos, emoji-as-icon) be scored reliably enough to act as an automated generation gate rather than a post-hoc complaint?
deep_dives.topic: AI slop as a measurable, gateable property
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Vibe-coded and AI-generated apps all look the same and share identical visual tells.
deep_dives.why: If homogenization is detectable, taste becomes a lintable property with thresholds and regressions, which is the precondition for treating design constraints like any other CI check. Without a detector, 'slop gates' remain a prompt-level wish.

evidence_quotes.text: Giving AI models structured design themes and anti-patterns dramatically improves output quality in a single prompt.
Provides a systemic programmatic defense against generic AI-generated user interfaces.
Giving AI models structured design themes and anti-patterns dramatically improves output quality in a single prompt.

deep_dives.research_question: Of anti-pattern gates, reference screenshots, and long voice-note-derived specs, which lever carries the observed quality gain, and do they compose additively or redundantly?
deep_dives.topic: Ablating the three taste levers: gates, references, and spec length
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Giving AI models structured design themes and anti-patterns dramatically improves output quality in a single prompt.
deep_dives.why: The workflow bundles three interventions and reports a single qualitative improvement. Teams cannot budget or tool the right lever without an ablation; the answer determines whether the durable artifact is a constraint file, an asset store, or an upstream spec capture step.

evidence_quotes.text: Introduces 'Hallmark', a design skill built to eliminate AI slop by codifying anti-patterns and providing structured design themes to AI models.
Giving AI models structured design themes and anti-patterns dramatically improves output quality in a single prompt.

deep_dives.research_question: Does an enumerated-anti-pattern pack retain its quality effect when moved from web aesthetics to a non-visual artifact (API schemas, error message voice, code structure), and when moved across model families?
deep_dives.topic: Portability of negative-constraint packs across domains and model families
deep_dives.trigger_insight: design skill built to eliminate AI slop
deep_dives.why: The mechanism claim is general but the evidence is scoped to landing pages on models named in a single talk. If constraint packs are model-idiosyncratic, the 'quality contract travels with the repo' argument collapses into per-model tuning debt.

evidence_quotes.text: Smaller, faster open-source models like GLM 5.2 can match or beat expensive closed models for UI iteration at a fraction of the cost.
Smaller open-source models can generate design outputs comparable to expensive closed models at 5x lower cost and higher speed.

deep_dives.research_question: On held-out UI tasks with blind human acceptance judgments, what is the win rate and cost ratio between a small open-source model and a frontier closed model, and does parity survive complex stateful UI beyond landing pages?
deep_dives.topic: Cost-per-accepted-change as the routing criterion for agent iteration loops
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Smaller, faster open-source models like GLM 5.2 can match or beat expensive closed models for UI iteration at a fraction of the cost.
deep_dives.why: Iteration is the high-frequency phase, so per-turn cost and latency dominate the loop's economics. A routing decision needs an acceptance-adjusted metric, not a token price or a single head-to-head on one task class, otherwise a weaker tier silently compounds mediocre decisions across turns.

evidence_quotes.text: Instead of demanding an entire app in one massive prompt, build the foundation and queue smaller incremental messages.
Queuing multiple incremental feature requests yields cleaner, more robust code and design than one monolithic prompt.

deep_dives.research_question: Does a foundation-first queue of small incremental requests reduce defect rates and improve design ratings versus single-shot generation when total token spend is held constant, and how much cross-step contradiction accumulates as the queue lengthens?
deep_dives.topic: Incremental milestone queues versus monolithic generation: coherence drift
deep_dives.why: Decomposition is claimed to produce cleaner code but introduces state re-reading, drift, and later steps contradicting earlier ones. The real engineering question is where the checkpoint and rollback boundary sits, not whether small steps are fashionable.

project_ideas.based_on: Vibe-coded and AI-generated apps all look the same and share identical visual tells.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A detector trained on the enumerated visual tells (purple gradient headers, italicized title words, three-card rows, fake testimonials, all-caps pill buttons, scroll-to-explore badges) can reject generated UI at a precision that reduces human-rated slop without suppressing legitimate uses of the same primitives.
project_ideas.measurement: Residual rate of banned tells per 100 generations; precision/recall of the detector against human labels; human aesthetic rating delta; false-positive rate on legitimately gradient/pill-based designs; agreement between detector score and blind human preference.
project_ideas.name: Slop Gate
project_ideas.poc: Assemble a labeled corpus of AI-generated and human-designed pages annotated for each tell; build a rubric-prompted scorer plus a lightweight classifier; wire it as a post-generation gate that either blocks, regenerates, or flags. Report residual banned-trope rate in constrained vs unconstrained generations across two model families.

project_ideas.based_on: Can 'AI slop' be measured objectively enough to serve as an automated gate or reward signal?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Anti-pattern gates account for a larger share of blind-rated quality improvement than reference screenshots or long specs, and the three levers are partly redundant rather than additive, so removing the weakest lever preserves quality at lower context cost.
project_ideas.measurement: Blind human win rate per arm against the null arm; marginal quality gain per added 1k tokens of context; variance of ratings across arms; cost per quality-adjusted generation.
project_ideas.name: Lever Ablation Bench
project_ideas.poc: Factorial design over identical build tasks: constraints only, references only, long voice-note-equivalent spec only, all combined, none. Freeze task prompts and model versions, gather blind pairwise human ratings, and hold total token budget constant across arms.

project_ideas.based_on: Concrete visual references outperform abstract style instructions
project_ideas.hypothesis: Treating admired screenshots as a retrievable, curated context asset — rather than ad-hoc pastes — produces measurable quality gains that persist when the reference and target differ substantially in layout, with diminishing returns beyond a small number of exemplars.
project_ideas.measurement: Blind-rated quality versus N (diminishing-returns curve); quality delta when reference layout similarity is low; attribution accuracy of which exemplar drove improvement; context-token overhead per gain.
project_ideas.name: Reference Vault
project_ideas.poc: Build a licensed, attributed screenshot store with tags and a retrieval step that injects N exemplars into generation; sweep N from 0 to 8 against layout-similar and layout-dissimilar reference sets; log which exemplar was active per generation for attribution.

project_ideas.based_on: Queuing multiple incremental feature requests yields cleaner, more robust code and design than one monolithic prompt.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A foundation-first queue of small incremental requests with per-step checkpoints reduces regression and cross-step contradiction rates versus single-shot generation at equal total token spend, and the benefit decays predictably as queue length grows.
project_ideas.measurement: Defect and regression count per build; cross-step contradiction rate versus queue length; rollback frequency; blind design rating; tokens spent per accepted milestone.
project_ideas.name: Milestone Queue Harness
project_ideas.poc: Implement an orchestration layer that owns an ordered milestone queue, re-reads accumulated state per step, verifies each step, and can roll back. Benchmark against a monolithic prompt on the same target apps with matched token budgets; log contradictions introduced per step.

source.title: The Missing Layer: Design Taste in AI Agents — Hassan El Mghari, Together AI

summary.html:
Overview

  • Speaker: Hassan El Mghari
  • Channel: AI Engineer
  • Main topic: How to make AI agent UIs look good and avoid AI slop
  • Purpose: To educate AI engineers and developers on how to improve the design and user interface of AI-generated applications by avoiding common AI design clichés and implementing structured design constraints. Hassan El Mghari, lead of the developer experience team at Together AI, discusses the problem of AI-generated applications shipping with ugly, homogeneous user interfaces known as AI slop. He shares his experience building 40+ AI apps reaching millions of users and outlines practical strategies for improving UI/UX design taste in AI-generated apps, introducing frameworks like Hallmark and recommending practices such as using references, longer prompts, and smaller, faster open-source models for iterative development.

Topic Map

Introduction and Background

  • Explanation: Hassan introduces himself, his role at Together AI, and his background in building successful AI web apps with millions of users, highlighting design and UX as the primary growth drivers.
  • Key claims:
    • Design and UX are the primary reasons why some AI apps get millions of users.
  • Examples:
    • LogoCreator
    • MakeComics
    • SubStudio
  • Terminology:
    • Together AI
    • Developer Experience
  • Why it matters: Establishes credibility in building popular AI applications and frames design as a competitive advantage.

The Problem of AI Slop in UI

  • Explanation: Identifies the common visual clichés and patterns that make vibe-coded and AI-generated apps look identical and cheap.
  • Key claims:
    • Vibe-coded and AI-generated apps all look the same and share identical visual tells.
  • Examples:
    • Purple gradient backgrounds
    • Italics in headers
    • Scroll to explore badges
    • All-caps pill buttons with dots
    • Gradient logos
    • Random emojis as icons
  • Terminology:
    • AI slop
    • vibe-coded apps
  • Why it matters: Recognizing AI visual clichés is the first step toward avoiding them and standing out competitively.

Hallmark and Design Skills

  • Explanation: Introduces 'Hallmark', a design skill built to eliminate AI slop by codifying anti-patterns and providing structured design themes to AI models.
  • Key claims:
    • Giving AI models structured design themes and anti-patterns dramatically improves output quality in a single prompt.
  • Examples:
    • Bubble theme
    • Distill theme
    • Cold Snap theme
    • Cinder theme
  • Terminology:
    • Hallmark
    • design skill
  • Why it matters: Provides a systemic programmatic defense against generic AI-generated user interfaces.

Model Selection for Iteration

  • Explanation: Compares using larger closed models against smaller open-source models like GLM 5.2 for rapid application iteration and design tuning.
  • Key claims:
    • Smaller, faster open-source models like GLM 5.2 can match or beat expensive closed models for UI iteration at a fraction of the cost.
  • Examples:
    • GLM 5.2 vs Opus 4.8 comparison on landing page generation
  • Terminology:
    • GLM 5.2
    • Opus 4.8
    • inference API
  • Why it matters: Optimizes cost and speed during iterative UI generation cycles without sacrificing visual quality.

Best Practices for AI Design Engineering

  • Explanation: Outlines actionable guidelines for developers to guide AI agents toward shipping high-quality UIs.
  • Key claims:
    • Using references, screenshots, longer prompts, and AGENTS.md configuration files radically improves AI design outputs.
  • Examples:
    • AGENTS.md
    • Voice notes for long prompts
    • Screenshot inspiration vaults
  • Terminology:
    • AGENTS.md
    • UX context
    • inspiration vault
  • Why it matters: Transforms amateur prompt engineering into a reliable design engineering workflow.

Key Points

AI slop is a major differentiator

  • Explanation: Most AI-generated apps share identical design patterns that instantly signal low effort and generic generation.
  • Evidence: Purple gradients, italicized header words, pills with all caps and dots, and random icons appear across most AI-built landing pages.
  • Practical implication: Investing 10-20% extra effort into design polish provides a massive competitive advantage.

Hallmark eliminates slop patterns

  • Explanation: Codifying design rules and anti-patterns into an AI skill file prevents models from using tired tropes.
  • Evidence: Hallmark explicitly refuses gradient headers, three-card rows, fake testimonials, purple glows, and italicized title words.
  • Practical implication: Embedding design constraints into your agent environment raises baseline aesthetics instantly.

Use references and screenshots instead of imagination

  • Explanation: AI models perform significantly better when given concrete visual examples rather than abstract stylistic instructions.
  • Evidence: Hassan's personal inspiration collection of high-quality app screenshots produces vastly superior results when fed to models.
  • Practical implication: Always feed your agent multiple reference screenshots of apps whose aesthetic you admire.

Write longer, highly specific prompts

  • Explanation: Short, vague prompts lead to generic output; multi-paragraph prompts or voice notes provide necessary UX context.
  • Evidence: Hassan records 2-3 minute voice notes detailing target user personas, UI components, and micro-interactions.
  • Practical implication: Treat agent prompting like writing detailed product specifications.

Break iteration into step-by-step queues

  • Explanation: Instead of demanding an entire app in one massive prompt, build the foundation and queue smaller incremental messages.
  • Evidence: Queuing multiple incremental feature requests yields cleaner, more robust code and design than one monolithic prompt.
  • Practical implication: Deconstruct app building into iterative prompt queues rather than single shot attempts.

Frameworks, Models & Processes

Hallmark

  • How it works: A design skill framework that defines strict anti-patterns (slop gates) and provides a curated library of professional themes as context to AI models.
  • Components:
    • Anti-slop gates (no purple gradients, no italicized headers, no fake testimonials)
    • Curated theme library (Bubble, Distill, Cold Snap, Cinder, etc.)
    • Single-prompt context injection
  • When to use: When prompting LLMs or coding agents to generate landing pages or web UIs.

Examples & Case Studies

Comparing GLM 5.2 and Opus 4.8 on landing page generation.

  • Illustrates: Smaller open-source models can generate design outputs comparable to expensive closed models at 5x lower cost and higher speed.
  • Lesson: Use smaller open-source models for fast UI iteration cycles.

Building LogoCreator and MakeComics as viral AI apps.

  • Illustrates: Simple, focused one-page apps with polished UI and animations can acquire tens of thousands of users.
  • Lesson: Design and UX are the main levers for user adoption in AI applications.

Actionable Takeaways

  • Immediate:
    • Stop using purple gradient backgrounds and italicized header words in AI-generated apps.
    • Provide reference screenshots and inspiration URLs to your AI agents.
    • Save your design preferences in an AGENTS.md file.
  • Strategic:
    • Treat AI agent outputs as a baseline foundation, not the final product.

## Overview
- **Speaker**: Hassan El Mghari
- **Channel**: AI Engineer
- **Main topic**: How to make AI agent UIs look good and avoid AI slop
- **Purpose**: To educate AI engineers and developers on how to improve the design and user interface of AI-generated applications by avoiding common AI design clichés and implementing structured design constraints.
Hassan El Mghari, lead of the developer experience team at Together AI, discusses the problem of AI-generated applications shipping with ugly, homogeneous user interfaces known as AI slop. He shares his experience building 40+ AI apps reaching millions of users and outlines practical strategies for improving UI/UX design taste in AI-generated apps, introducing frameworks like Hallmark and recommending practices such as using references, longer prompts, and smaller, faster open-source models for iterative development.
## Topic Map
### Introduction and Background
- **Explanation**: Hassan introduces himself, his role at Together AI, and his background in building successful AI web apps with millions of users, highlighting design and UX as the primary growth drivers.
- **Key claims**:
  - Design and UX are the primary reasons why some AI apps get millions of users.
- **Examples**:
  - LogoCreator
  - MakeComics
  - SubStudio
- **Terminology**:
  - Together AI
  - Developer Experience
- **Why it matters**: Establishes credibility in building popular AI applications and frames design as a competitive advantage.
### The Problem of AI Slop in UI
- **Explanation**: Identifies the common visual clichés and patterns that make vibe-coded and AI-generated apps look identical and cheap.
- **Key claims**:
  - Vibe-coded and AI-generated apps all look the same and share identical visual tells.
- **Examples**:
  - Purple gradient backgrounds
  - Italics in headers
  - Scroll to explore badges
  - All-caps pill buttons with dots
  - Gradient logos
  - Random emojis as icons
- **Terminology**:
  - AI slop
  - vibe-coded apps
- **Why it matters**: Recognizing AI visual clichés is the first step toward avoiding them and standing out competitively.
### Hallmark and Design Skills
- **Explanation**: Introduces 'Hallmark', a design skill built to eliminate AI slop by codifying anti-patterns and providing structured design themes to AI models.
- **Key claims**:
  - Giving AI models structured design themes and anti-patterns dramatically improves output quality in a single prompt.
- **Examples**:
  - Bubble theme
  - Distill theme
  - Cold Snap theme
  - Cinder theme
- **Terminology**:
  - Hallmark
  - design skill
- **Why it matters**: Provides a systemic programmatic defense against generic AI-generated user interfaces.
### Model Selection for Iteration
- **Explanation**: Compares using larger closed models against smaller open-source models like GLM 5.2 for rapid application iteration and design tuning.
- **Key claims**:
  - Smaller, faster open-source models like GLM 5.2 can match or beat expensive closed models for UI iteration at a fraction of the cost.
- **Examples**:
  - GLM 5.2 vs Opus 4.8 comparison on landing page generation
- **Terminology**:
  - GLM 5.2
  - Opus 4.8
  - inference API
- **Why it matters**: Optimizes cost and speed during iterative UI generation cycles without sacrificing visual quality.
### Best Practices for AI Design Engineering
- **Explanation**: Outlines actionable guidelines for developers to guide AI agents toward shipping high-quality UIs.
- **Key claims**:
  - Using references, screenshots, longer prompts, and AGENTS.md configuration files radically improves AI design outputs.
- **Examples**:
  - AGENTS.md
  - Voice notes for long prompts
  - Screenshot inspiration vaults
- **Terminology**:
  - AGENTS.md
  - UX context
  - inspiration vault
- **Why it matters**: Transforms amateur prompt engineering into a reliable design engineering workflow.
## Key Points
### AI slop is a major differentiator
- **Explanation**: Most AI-generated apps share identical design patterns that instantly signal low effort and generic generation.
- **Evidence**: Purple gradients, italicized header words, pills with all caps and dots, and random icons appear across most AI-built landing pages.
- **Practical implication**: Investing 10-20% extra effort into design polish provides a massive competitive advantage.
### Hallmark eliminates slop patterns
- **Explanation**: Codifying design rules and anti-patterns into an AI skill file prevents models from using tired tropes.
- **Evidence**: Hallmark explicitly refuses gradient headers, three-card rows, fake testimonials, purple glows, and italicized title words.
- **Practical implication**: Embedding design constraints into your agent environment raises baseline aesthetics instantly.
### Use references and screenshots instead of imagination
- **Explanation**: AI models perform significantly better when given concrete visual examples rather than abstract stylistic instructions.
- **Evidence**: Hassan's personal inspiration collection of high-quality app screenshots produces vastly superior results when fed to models.
- **Practical implication**: Always feed your agent multiple reference screenshots of apps whose aesthetic you admire.
### Write longer, highly specific prompts
- **Explanation**: Short, vague prompts lead to generic output; multi-paragraph prompts or voice notes provide necessary UX context.
- **Evidence**: Hassan records 2-3 minute voice notes detailing target user personas, UI components, and micro-interactions.
- **Practical implication**: Treat agent prompting like writing detailed product specifications.
### Break iteration into step-by-step queues
- **Explanation**: Instead of demanding an entire app in one massive prompt, build the foundation and queue smaller incremental messages.
- **Evidence**: Queuing multiple incremental feature requests yields cleaner, more robust code and design than one monolithic prompt.
- **Practical implication**: Deconstruct app building into iterative prompt queues rather than single shot attempts.
## Frameworks, Models & Processes
### Hallmark
- **How it works**: A design skill framework that defines strict anti-patterns (slop gates) and provides a curated library of professional themes as context to AI models.
- **Components**:
  - Anti-slop gates (no purple gradients, no italicized headers, no fake testimonials)
  - Curated theme library (Bubble, Distill, Cold Snap, Cinder, etc.)
  - Single-prompt context injection
- **When to use**: When prompting LLMs or coding agents to generate landing pages or web UIs.
## Examples & Case Studies
### Comparing GLM 5.2 and Opus 4.8 on landing page generation.
- **Illustrates**: Smaller open-source models can generate design outputs comparable to expensive closed models at 5x lower cost and higher speed.
- **Lesson**: Use smaller open-source models for fast UI iteration cycles.

- **Illustrates**: Simple, focused one-page apps with polished UI and animations can acquire tens of thousands of users.
- **Lesson**: Design and UX are the main levers for user adoption in AI applications.

  - Save your design preferences in an AGENTS.md file.
